title: 在使用高回报率鼠标时，无界鼠标会变得特别卡顿

judgment.rationale: The reporter supplied a concrete high-polling trigger and confirmed Mouse Without Borders, which is enough for a maintainer reproduction attempt. The polling-rate sensitivity suggests event-volume or forwarding pressure but does not identify a code-level cause.
evidence: The original report names PowerToys 0.96.0 and describes severe lag/ghosting on the controlled machine when an 8000 Hz mouse is used across two laptops connected by Mouse Without Borders over Wi-Fi 6.
A maintainer asked whether the affected module was Mouse Without Borders; the reporter confirmed yes.
The live issue has no assignee. Its Product-Mouse Utilities label conflicts with the clarified Mouse Without Borders module.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce on current supported PowerToys and compare 125/1000/8000 Hz polling while holding the same two-machine Mouse Without Borders setup constant.

fix_assessment.rationale: A maintainer reproduction can determine whether the high-polling trigger is within Mouse Without Borders before selecting a fix.

proposed_fixes.title: Keep Mouse Without Borders responsive with high-polling mice
proposed_fixes.root_cause: A low-confidence hypothesis is that high-rate mouse input creates more forwarding work than the receiving path can drain; no timing or queue measurements are available.
plan: Reproduce on the current supported build with the same two-machine setup and compare 125, 1000 and 8000 Hz polling rates.
Measure sender/receiver input rates, forwarding delay and queue/backlog behavior; verify the problem follows Mouse Without Borders rather than a local mouse driver or network path.
If the MWB forwarding path is the bottleneck, make a bounded coalescing or scheduling change and add a high-rate regression test without dropping required input events.
verification: The reproduction distinguishes normal polling from the reported 8000 Hz lag/ghosting.
Mouse movement remains responsive on the receiving machine at high polling without unbounded queued work.
Normal polling, button events and other Mouse Without Borders features continue to work.

confidence.rationale: The author clarified the module and trigger, but the symptom has not been reproduced or attributed to a forwarding path.

reproduce.title: Measure Mouse Without Borders responsiveness at high polling rates
reproduce.version_requirement: Compare the reported PowerToys 0.96.0 behavior with the current supported build.
prerequisites: Two Windows PCs connected through Mouse Without Borders.
A mouse configurable for 8000 Hz polling, with polling rate measurable or selectable.
steps: Record the MWB configuration and test a stable connection with the mouse at 125 Hz.
Repeat the same remote movement at 1000 Hz and 8000 Hz while recording visible lag/ghosting and input-forwarding delay.
Keep the remote machine, connection and workload constant; compare whether the lag follows the polling rate and whether it is present in local input.
reproduce.expected_result: The high-polling trigger is either reproduced specifically in Mouse Without Borders or separated from local driver/network effects.
